deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Systèmes d'hyperplans (projectifs) réels'. This page sets up the combinatorics of a real central hyperplane arrangement, which serves as preparation for 'systèmes de pseudo-droites' (pseudo-line arrangements).

Set-up. V is a real vector space and H a hyperplane. D_H = {H, V'_H, V''_H} is the partition of V into H and its two open half-spaces. It is a 3-element set with a distinguished element H, so it can be viewed as an F_3-line with H = 0 and the half-spaces = ±1. This is in fact canonical: a 3-element pointed set carries a unique F_3-vector-space structure, so negation (swapping the half-spaces) is intrinsic and no orientation needs to be chosen.

Sign map. For S = V*/R_{>0} (the sphere of rays), there is a sign map φ_H : S → D_H. For a finite family (H_i)_{i∈I} this gives φ : S → E = ∏ D_{H_i} ≅ F_3^I. The nonempty fibres Z*_α partition S into relatively open convex cells (open convex cones upstairs). Σ = φ(S) ⊂ E is the set of sign vectors realized, which today is the set of covectors of the associated oriented matroid. Σ is stable under -id_E, with Z*_{-α} = -Z*_α.

Goal. The stated aim is to determine the closures of the cells. The next page answers this: the closure of Z*_α is the union of the Z*_β with β ≤ α in the product of the orders 0 < ±1. So the closure relation is the face-poset order with its Alexandrov ('infimum') topology. In modern terms, this is the face poset / covector lattice of an arrangement as a regular cell decomposition of the sphere.

Margins:
- The affine case is analogous and reduces to the projective one.
- 'Distinct' is unnecessary; repeated hyperplanes can be allowed.
- The convexity / cell claim fails unless ∩H_i = {0}. Otherwise the zero fibre is a sphere, and every cell contains the lineality space.

Purpose: an axiomatic or combinatorial basis, via sign vectors in F_3^I, for generalizing to pseudo-line / pseudo-hyperplane systems. This is the oriented-matroid programme.
errors: Notational inconsistency: D_H is defined as a partition of V, but φ_H is defined on S = V*/R*+, and the cones live 'dans V*'. Either the H_i should be hyperplanes of V*, or S should be (V∖0)/R*+. The text is consistent up to duality, but as written it mixes V and V*.
The claim that the fibres are convex (cells) requires ∩H_i = {0}. Otherwise the fibre over 0 is a sphere and is not convex in S. Grothendieck himself flags this in the bottom-left margin.
'V* ∪ {0}' inserted text: the inverse image of a fibre is an open convex cone; adding 0 only applies to the closed or zero cell. Minor.

ideas.what: Encode each hyperplane's three-piece partition as an F_3-line and the arrangement by sign vectors in F_3^I.
ideas.modern_name: Sign vectors / covectors of a realizable oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bland, Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence (1975–78); sign-vector viewpoint also Edmonds–Mandel

ideas.what: The set Σ of realized sign vectors is symmetric under negation, matching the antipodal map on cells.
ideas.modern_name: Covector symmetry axiom (V1) of oriented matroids

ideas.what: Remark that a pointed 3-element set is canonically an F_3-line, so negation is intrinsic and no orientation of the hyperplanes is needed.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical F_3 structure / unoriented sign data

ideas.what: Closure of cells = down-set in the product order 0<±; Alexandrov topology on Σ (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of an arrangement; regular CW decomposition of the sphere; Alexandrov topology of a poset

missed.claim: Historical: from 1981 on, Grothendieck independently began developing the sign-vector (F_3) formalism of hyperplane and pseudo-line arrangements, i.e. oriented-matroid covector theory, apparently unaware of Folkman–Lawrence and Bland–Las Vergnas. This page is the realizable starting point and contains no new mathematics, but the dossier documents an unrecorded episode in the prehistory/parallel history of oriented matroids.
missed.quote: on peut regarder D_H comme un espace vectoriel sur F_3={-1,0,1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest only. It credits Grothendieck with independent work on oriented matroids and pseudo-line systems, which the oriented-matroid literature does not mention.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard set-up of the face poset and sign vectors of a real arrangement, correct apart from a flagged genericity condition. Only the historical fact of Grothendieck independently entering oriented-matroid territory is noteworthy.
transcription_corrections: The insertion next to D_H reads '⊂ 𝔓(V)' (power set of V, since D_H is a set of subsets of V), not '⊂ ℙ(V)' (projective space).
Last line: should read 'On se propose de déterminer \overline{Z^*_\alpha} pour α∈Σ' (closure of the cell, as computed on the next page), not 'Σ*_α pour i∈I'.
Top-left margin is roughly: 'Théorie analogue dans le cas affine, mais qui se ramène au cas projectif ... des H_i distincts'.
Bottom-left margin concerns the convexity of the cells failing unless ∩H_i = {0}.
